summary: Short-term-rental operators with several units in different cities risk fines and delistings from missed permit renewals and rule changes, and there is a price gap between $27/property and $199+/month tools. Demand is only one forum thread, so run a $0 landing-page test before building.

demand.evidence: One BiggerPockets thread (RESEARCH.md source 1); no payer or behavior. Indirect: paying competitors (MyLodgeTax $27/property/mo, HostReady $199+/mo) and real enforcement (Las Vegas $72,900 fine).

statusQuo.evidence: Spreadsheet plus calendar reminders; nobody watches ordinance pages. Cost is fines of $500-$10,000+ per violation (Hostaway) or a delisted client listing. Dates alone are well covered by a spreadsheet.

specificity.evidence: Independent co-host or small manager with 3-15 units in 2-5 jurisdictions, paid per unit managed. A role with a concrete consequence, but no named person and no interviews; segment unsized.

wedge.evidence: Ordinance-change diffs at a flat price are the sellable wedge; reminders alone are undifferentiated. Hand-run 10 ordinance watches for the first signups before building.

futureFit.evidence: More jurisdictions and rule churn (EU 2024/1028 from May 2026, Houston, Austin) raise the value of tracking; PMSs (Hostaway) and HostReady moving down-market are the threat.

premises: Operators with 3-15 units across several jurisdictions are a reachable, paying segment (weakly supported, unsized)
Fear of a missed renewal is strong enough to pay $19/mo over a free spreadsheet (unproven)
Ordinance-change diffs, not reminders, are the paid wedge (reasonable, but they are M2)
A reminder-only tool with no filing earns trust (open)
Ordinance pages can be fetched and diffed cheaply (partly; many are PDFs or JS-rendered)
alternatives: Minimal: landing page plus concierge, with David hand-running ordinance watches for the first signups (recommended)
M1 as specced: reminder tracker with ICS feed (builds the least differentiated part first)
Ideal: curated jurisdiction library with ordinance watch, priced per city (best moat, manual and stale-prone)
Lateral: paid rule-change newsletter for 10 cities (a Whop STR Compliance Hub already exists)
No existing David repo fits; only RepoHQ's idea-signal pipeline is reused for the landing page
wedge: A landing page plus one sample ordinance-diff email, then a hand-run ordinance watch for the first signups at a flat $19/mo.

feasibility.notes: Next.js on Vercel Hobby, Turso or Supabase free, Resend free, cron on Actions or Vercel; no LLM, vercel.app subdomain. Test: dueReminders for a permit expiring 2026-12-31 returns the 90-day reminder on 2026-10-02 and none on 2026-10-03, and running the job twice sends each reminder once.

risks: Demand rests on one forum thread and no payer has been interviewed
Reminder-only M1 is not better than a spreadsheet and calendar
PDF and JS-rendered ordinance pages break naive hashing
Alert errors invite legal blame; needs a disclaimer and a source link
Jurisdiction data is manual and goes stale
HostReady or a PMS adds a low tier
At $19/mo it takes about 50 customers for $1k/mo
killCriteria: After 14 days and 50+ qualified visitors, fewer than 5 signups state 3+ properties; or fewer than 3 of 10 interviewed operators would pay $19/mo; or most target ordinance pages can't be fetched and diffed reliably.

landing.headline: Never miss an STR permit renewal or a city rule change
landing.subhead: Permit and lodging-tax deadlines for every property, plus an emailed diff when a city ordinance page changes. One flat price, no per-property fees.
bullets: Email reminders 90, 60, 30 and 7 days before each permit and tax deadline
Ordinance watch: see exactly which lines changed on your city's page
All deadlines in your Google or Apple calendar
Flat monthly price for 3-15 properties, not per property
landing.audience: Co-hosts and small property managers running 3-15 short-term rentals across 2+ cities
